intended_object: The forgetful map that sends a σ-semilinear map f : M₁ → M₂ to the same function, seen as an additive monoid homomorphism M₁ →+ M₂. This comes from the docstring "Convert a linear map to an additive monoid hom".
explanation:
The body keeps the underlying function f and proves that it preserves 0 and addition using the linear map's own lemmas (`f.map_zero` and `f.map_add`). So it is exactly the underlying additive homomorphism of the semilinear map.

The generality is already the natural one: semilinear maps over any ring homomorphism σ between semirings, on any additive commutative monoids. Mathlib also has a generic coercion that sends any `AddMonoidHomClass` morphism to an additive monoid homomorphism (`AddMonoidHom.ofClass`, the additive counterpart of `MonoidHom.ofClass`). That is not a sign the definition is too narrow: this is the standard specialised projection for linear maps, it gives the same result, and it applies in the full generality where linear maps make sense.
